title: UI Conventions
intro: MTG Arena is the reference for Beryl's flow, the order and timing of events, table layout and wording (AGENTS.md, UI; [Project 50k](project-50k.md), K22). This page lists only what Arena does not settle: where Beryl differs on purpose, what Arena has no equivalent for, and what the recordings do not show.

The rulings were made on 2026-11-10 from an audit of 180 bug reports against the recordings in `~/arena`. Each Arena finding cites the recording moments that show it, as `<recording id> <time>`, for `just video film`.
This page is generated from `data/ui-conventions.json` (K28) by `just conventions`: edit the data, not the page. The repo lane fails when the page is stale.

sections.heading: Beryl exceptions
intro: Beryl does these and Arena does not. A bug report from the user adds, changes or removes an entry; nothing else does.

sections.heading: Settled as Arena
intro: Arena's way stands where an earlier report asked for something else, so do not restore the old behavior.

sections.heading: Not seen in Arena
intro: Built from motions and shapes Beryl already has. Arena has these, but the recordings do not show them.

sections.heading: Still open
intro: To be settled from the recordings (Project 50k, presentation track). Until then the current behavior stays.

lists.heading: Verbs
intro: Every change on the table is shown by one of these, applied to a card, an ability or a player by a step of the script the session sends (`rust/crates/beryl_session/src/script`, K23). The list is closed: what Arena does not show is composed from these. A verb's duration, delay, stagger and curve, and each case's, are the values below, which `just motion` holds the stage to; Arena's measured instances are kept beside them as reference in `data/arena-motion.json` (K27).

lists.heading: Effects
intro: An effect is light or a change of surface on one card or one player's life total, begun by a step of a verb as it starts, as it ends or as its blow lands and played on the stage's clock (`ui/src/stage/effects.ts`): it never moves a card and never holds up the script. The list is closed, each effect has one look in Beryl's skin (`ui/src/stage/stage.css`), and a verb names the effects its steps begin. A mark says what a player may do; an effect says what just happened, and is gone.

lists.heading: Marks
intro: A mark is the only highlight a card, an ability or a player carries, in a script or in a prompt (K26). The list is closed, and each mark has one look. What a card's own state says (tapped, summoning sick, counters, attacking) is its face, not a mark.

entries.name: Phase icons
entries.rule: Twelve icons, two rows of three on each side of the life total, filled where a stop is set, the same rows for both seats.

arena.does: Arena shows one row above the action button.

entries.name: Full cards that tap
entries.rule: A permanent is its whole card and turns when it taps.

arena.does: Arena shows a crop of the art.

entries.name: No question before a choice
entries.rule: Never ask a yes or no whose answer the next screen could take: open the search, chooser or payment with a way to decline.

arena.does: Arena asks "Search your library…?" first.

entries.name: Target arrows by relationship
entries.rule: Red at something an opponent controls, green at your own. This is skin, listed so nobody removes it.

arena.does: Arena draws every target arrow cyan, whoever controls either end; its one red line is an opponent's declared attack, with a red chevron under the attacker.

entries.name: Lands unstacked until seven
entries.rule: Each land is separate until its controller has seven or more; then same-named lands stack.

arena.does: Arena piles same-named lands from the second copy, a tapped pile apart from an untapped one, and a pile of four shows "x4".

entries.name: Linked exile under its host
entries.rule: A card exiled "until this leaves the battlefield" sits tucked under the permanent that exiled it.

arena.does: Arena shows no link on the table.

entries.name: Own-target warning
entries.rule: Confirm before a counter or removal spell targets the player's own spell or permanent.

entries.name: Lines and combat marks of light
entries.rule: Arrows, lines of combat and the marks of combat are painted as light, in Beryl's colors. An attacker wears a wedge of ember light on its leading edge, which pops as it is declared and turns gold once it is blocked; a blocker has a gold crescent under it and a gold beam to the tip of its attacker's wedge. The lines and marks of combat lie on the table, under the cards and the step's banner ("it looks a bit dumb in places" over them); only an arrow at a target and the line to a source are drawn over what rests. An arrow strikes and drains where Arena's appears and is cut. This replaces the thin flat lines and pale gold marks, which read as a diagram: "crummy and cartoony". The line a declaration pulls toward the pointer follows the pointer itself, with no lag.

arena.does: A target arrow is a cyan ribbon of light that appears whole in one frame and is cut as its spell resolves. An attacker's chevron appears in one frame, a little wide and bright, and settles; it is red, and gold once blocked. A blocker's line is a gold beam with a head and a crescent under the blocker, cut as combat damage begins.

entries.name: Tokens
entries.rule: They appear at their slot; they do not fly out of their source.

arena.does: Arena's appears whole with a short glow, about 0.1 s after its ability leaves the stack; a batch appears as one group.

entries.name: Permanents that leave
entries.rule: A permanent that is not a token dissolves where it is: destroyed, it breaks into ash at its slot; exiled, it becomes a vortex there. Nothing flies to the pile. What it leaves room for closes up only once it has gone.

arena.does: A destroyed creature glows and falls to ash over about 1 s; the spell then goes to its graveyard. The row closes up after the permanent is gone.

entries.name: Choosing how to cast
entries.rule: A card or permanent with more than one way to cast or use it opens a modal, "Choose One", showing the card once per option, with Cancel: an adventure, an alternative cost, a land's abilities.

arena.does: Brazen Borrower, Bonecrusher Giant and Force of Will open it from hand, Wasteland on the battlefield.

entries.name: A finished ability
entries.rule: It is removed at once, with no fade.

entries.name: Wording
entries.rule: Arena's exactly, case and punctuation too: "All Attack", "Choose attackers." Every prompt's title and buttons are one table in the session (`rust/crates/beryl_session/src/prompt/wording.rs`), each entry beside the recording moments that show it. A browser's title is the line that asks: its sentence of rules text, or its heading where the line under it only says how to drag. A pick is confirmed by "Submit" and the number picked, an arrangement by "Done", a "may" by "Take Action" or "Decline".

entries.name: Button order
entries.rule: It follows Arena prompt by prompt; there is no blanket "default on the right".

entries.name: The opponent's turn
entries.rule: Arena's "Opponent's Turn" label shows in the action button's place, and no spinner.

entries.name: Attacking a planeswalker
entries.rule: No prompt: an attacker defaults to the player, and the player pulls an arrow to the planeswalker.

arena.does: Attackers that can attack get a cyan outline; a clicked attacker turns gold, the opponent's life total and the planeswalker glow, and an arrow follows the cursor to the planeswalker.

entries.name: Two items on the stack
entries.rule: The top one still gets its target arrow. Each item beneath peeks out to the left of the one over it by a quarter of its width (a fifth past five items, as far as the room left of the stack allows), so a spell leaving from under another is seen as it goes.

arena.does: A cyan arc runs from the top item to its target, even when that is the one card under it; the top card sits a little right of and below the one beneath, which shows about a third of its width beside it, and a countered spell crumbles in that strip.

entries.name: Additional costs
entries.rule: A chooser that lowers the mana to pay (Delve) opens before mana taps; a sacrifice cost is chosen after the lands tap.

arena.does: Treasure Cruise's Delve chooser opens before any land taps; Natural Order's lands send their mana, then "Sacrifice a green creature." opens.

entries.name: Choosing X
entries.rule: The value of X is set by a step down and a step up beside it, over the button that answers, which says the value under its label: "Pay" over "X = 1". Beside the value stands the whole cost it makes, and the permanents that would pay it are outlined as the value changes. Beryl has the single steps alone.

arena.does: Mind Twist's X stands under the spell between -5, - and +, +5, on a button that reads Pay over X = 0, with Cancel.

entries.name: Dividing among targets
entries.rule: Each target wears its share on its card, between a step that raises it and a step that lowers it, under the arrow to it; "Submit" answers once everything is given out. The prompt says after what it asks how much is still to give, as a cost paid with permanents says what is left.

arena.does: Fire Covenant's damage: an arrow from the spell to each target, a count on each between an arrow up and an arrow down, Submit and Cancel.

entries.name: Choosing from a list
entries.rule: The entries stand in a column over the shaded table. A press lights an entry and "Submit 1" answers with it, where Arena takes a color at the press: no card asks for an entry yet, and the prompt is the one a longer list needs, a creature type or a card name.

arena.does: Mother of Runes' color: Choose One over Choose Color, and White, Blue, Black, Red and Green in a column, each taken at a click.

entries.name: A countered spell
entries.rule: It leaves before the spell that countered it.

arena.does: The countered spell crumbles in place under the counterspell, which stays until the debris is gone and then fades, 0.5 to 0.9 s later.

entries.name: Cards the opponent looks at
entries.rule: They come off the top of their library face down at library size and lie beside it; a top-bound card slides back onto the library and a bottom-bound one slides away from it, to either side. A pill above their avatar reads "Scry: 1 top, 1 bottom." for about 3 s.

arena.does: No card is enlarged.

entries.name: A line from an ability to its source
entries.rule: It is always shown while the ability is on the stack, thin and faint as Arena draws it, and hidden during a prompt. A heavy arrow is not that line.

entries.name: Passing to the end step
entries.rule: "End Turn" passes until the end step, but stops when the opponent puts a spell or ability on the stack: the button reads "Resolve", then "Pass" once it resolves.

arena.does: The button reads "End Turn" over "To End", and goes blank while it passes.

entries.name: Targeting a spell
entries.rule: With one spell on the stack, a spell that targets a spell takes it with no prompt and no Confirm. With more, a "Choose One" browser of the stack, "Target a spell.", opens with nothing preselected, Submit and Cancel.

arena.does: Counterspell and Mana Leak at a lone spell go straight onto the stack; Spell Pierce over two spells opens the browser at "Submit 0".

entries.name: Mana into what it pays for
entries.rule: Each tapped land glows and sends one streak of its color straight to the spell on the stack, which flashes as they land, in about 0.3 s. Mana does not stop at a pool.

arena.does: Seen for casts paid with lands.

entries.name: The local player's scry
entries.rule: The table is shaded and "Scry" shows the cards face up over it, BOTTOM on the left and TOP on the right, and Done; surveil's has Graveyard and Library boxes instead. The cards are the library's own: they come up from it as the prompt opens, and on Done the shade lifts at once and they go back to it at its size, none shown large on its way to the top or the bottom. A pill reads "Scry: 1 top, 1 bottom."

arena.does: Seen for a scry of two and for surveil; no card changes face.

entries.name: A card a look puts in the graveyard
entries.rule: It appears on the graveyard at pile size once the chooser closes; it is not shown large first.

arena.does: A surveilled card lands on the graveyard as the overlay closes; kept cards close with the overlay.

entries.name: A batch exile
entries.rule: Cards exiled together leave one at a time, about 0.3 s apart.

arena.does: Delve's cards gather on the graveyard, then peel off its top one by one into a vortex. Delve is the only batch exile in the recordings, all in one recording.

entries.name: An opponent's spell returned to hand
entries.rule: It breaks up in place on the stack over 0.5 to 1 s; it does not fly or flip toward their hand.

arena.does: Seen for Remand on the opponent's spells.

entries.name: Hover inspection
entries.rule: A hovered card in hand rises and grows in place to about twice its size. A hovered permanent gets a separate copy about three times its size, away from the cursor, with its keywords explained. A card on the stack gets none.

arena.does: Estimated from stills, not measured.

entries.name: Undo
entries.rule: Every answer can be undone, across turns and prompts, the cast and its payment together.

entries.name: Chrome
entries.rule: Round icon buttons; the log toggle top left; the bug button above undo with no gap kept for a missing button.

entries.name: Why a click is refused
entries.rule: An illegal click shows its reason at the permanent that forbids it.

entries.name: Suggestions are sensible
entries.rule: The suggested untap targets and the auto-pay sources are the ones a player would pick.

entries.name: Nothing overlaps
entries.rule: The hand, the stack and their indicators never cover a control or each other. No layer of a library, graveyard or exile pile covers a card in play, for either seat, however long a row grows. The opponent's piles keep the band above their back row to themselves.

entries.name: Paying with permanents
entries.rule: Waterbend, convoke, crew. Start with no payment highlights. Hover over Auto Pay on desktop or long-press it on mobile to see which permanents Beryl would use. Click or tap the button to accept. To pay manually, click or tap each permanent you want to contribute. For a three-creature Convoke, pick A, B and D directly even if Auto Pay would use A, B and C. After each manual pick, recalculate the proposal for the remaining cost and keep the player's picks. Let the player finish manually or accept Auto Pay for the remainder, and stop taking picks once the cost is covered. Arena documents the preview and acceptance gestures in its [May 23, 2019 patch notes](https://devtrackers.gg/magic-arena/p/3e5941f1-may-23-0-15-00-00-patch-notes). A selected permanent turns and carries a tap mark, and an outline means one thing at a time: at rest every permanent that can pay wears the outline of what may be picked, and while Auto Pay shows its proposal those it would tap alone show, in their ring. The prompt says after what it asks how much is still to pay.

entries.name: A creature that enters attacking
entries.rule: It gets an explicit choice of what it attacks, and its line stays drawn throughout.

entries.name: A token that leaves
entries.rule: It dissolves in place like any permanent. No token leaving the battlefield is seen.

entries.name: Evoke and cycling
entries.rule: A card with evoke, or a land with cycling, opens the same "Choose One" modal. No evoke is seen; Triomes cycle straight to the stack, but whether a land could still be played is not shown.

arena.does: Arena shows no chooser before these cycles.

entries.name: Known cards in a library
entries.rule: A known top card shows face up on its library, and clicking a library lists its known cards. No known card in the opponent's library is seen.

arena.does: The player's own library stays a card back after their tutor puts a card on top, and after a look.

entries.name: A card turning face up
entries.rule: A face-down permanent turning face up enlarges in place and flips; one leaving reveals its face during its flight, and one that leaves for a hand or a library, where no face shows, joins the Revealed Cards as it goes. Nothing turns face up in the recordings, and one face-down card is seen leaving.

arena.does: Killed, Arena's face-down card dissolves as a card back and a "Revealed Cards" panel then shows its face at the top left.

entries.name: Cards a look returns
entries.rule: Cards a look puts back into a library fly straight to it. No look at several cards with the rest returned is filmed.

entries.name: A linked exile returning
entries.rule: The exiled card returns as its source departs, moving with it. No exiling permanent is seen leaving with its card returning.

entries.name: Your own spell returned to hand
entries.rule: It glides from the stack to the hand, turning as it goes. Only the opponent's spells are seen returned.

entries.name: The opponent's draws and discards
entries.rule: A card the opponent draws flies face down from their library to their hand, as long as any card flies and never spinning round on the way. One they discard flies to their graveyard and turns face up on the way, as their spells do. Only the player's own are seen.

entries.name: A mulligan's hand
entries.rule: It goes from sight where it lies, every card of it, as a permanent that leaves does; then the next hand is dealt as an opening hand is. No mulligan is filmed.

entries.name: Milled cards
entries.rule: They fly from the library to the graveyard face up, one after another as draws do. None is held up large first. No mill is seen.

entries.name: The Revealed Cards between reveals
entries.rule: The pile holds what one spell or ability revealed, and what another reveals takes its place; a card revealed and then put where its face shows (a graveyard, exile, the battlefield, the stack) is not held up, since its flight shows it. The pile opens into the viewer every pile opens into. The recordings show the pile with one effect's cards at a time, dismissed before the next.

arena.does: One spell's four revealed cards lie in the pile together; the next reveal seen comes after the pile was dismissed.

entries.name: Cards leaving a graveyard
entries.rule: A card returned to the battlefield or to a hand flies there from its pile. None is seen.

entries.name: An ability with no source on the battlefield
entries.rule: It emerges from the pile its source lies in, and appears on the stack when it has no source. No trigger from a graveyard is seen.

entries.name: A cost paid as a spell resolves
entries.rule: Mana streaks from its sources into the resolving spell or ability, as into a spell being cast. No such payment is seen.

entries.name: Mana spent from a pool
entries.rule: It streaks from its player's pool into the spell or ability it pays for, as from a land. No floating mana is seen.

entries.name: A target that moves
entries.rule: An arrow or line ends before either of its ends moves, and an arrow is not drawn again at a card that changed zones while its spell or ability stays on the stack. No target is seen leaving in response.

entries.name: A copy on the stack
entries.rule: It appears on the stack with no flight. None is seen.

entries.name: A permanent changing sides
entries.rule: It flies across the battlefield to its new controller's row.

arena.does: Seen only before and after its move

entries.name: Equipment
entries.rule: It flies to the creature it becomes attached to.

arena.does: The equip ability leaves the stack with a flash at the creature; the equipment's own move is not seen

entries.name: Other numbers
entries.rule: A changed power and toughness, and mana left in a pool, count as a life total does. Neither is seen.

entries.name: Words: what a card's text would say
entries.rule: Arena words many prompts from the text of the card that asks, which a prompt's record does not carry. Beryl says what Arena says of any card, or the same sentence less the card's part: "Choose a target.", "Search for a card.", "Search your library?", "Exile a card.", "Exile {most:words} cards.", "Distribute damage.", "Distribute counters.", "Choose One" over a card chosen for an effect, and an optional effect under its asker's name ("{source}", or "Take Action?" with none). Braces are the table's holes.

arena.does: Arena names the card's own: Target a creature., Search for a basic land card., Exile a blue card., Draw a card?

entries.name: Words: prompts Beryl folds
entries.rule: Where Arena asks before a choice, Beryl opens the choice (exception 3) and words it from both screens. One discard in place of several: "Discard a basic land card or {most:words} cards." A look that may take nothing is its sentence as a question, with "Decline": "Put {most:words} of them into your hand?", "Exile {most:words} of them?", "Put {most:words} of them into your library?", "Put {most:words} of them into your graveyard?", "Put {most:words} of them onto the battlefield?". The other way about, Arena opens a payment that may be declined and Beryl asks first: "Pay {cost}." is answered "Pay {cost}" or "Decline". A card offered to cast is cast by its button, "Cast".

arena.does: Arena asks Discard a basic land card? and then Discard two cards.; a look that may take nothing is headed Choose One over a question, with Submit and Decline; a payment that may be declined has Decline beside Auto Pay.

entries.name: Words: prompts the recordings lack
entries.rule: Each is composed from the nearest prompt Arena shows. A discard to hand size: "Discard {most} cards." A mulligan of more than one card: "Return {most} Cards". Manifest dread: "Manifest one of them." Cards put back from a hand: "Put a card on top.", "Put {most:words} cards on top." A fateseal: "Top of Library", answered "BOTTOM" or "TOP" as a scry's piles are named. A card that goes on top or bottom with no asker to name: "Top or Bottom?". Looked-at cards sent to a graveyard or the battlefield: "Put {most:words} of them into your graveyard.", "Put {most:words} of them onto the battlefield." An optional move of a card anywhere but to exile: "Put that card into your hand{from}?", "Put that card into your graveyard{from}?", "Put that card onto the battlefield{from}?", "Put that card into your library{from}?", "Move that card{from}?". A cost of no mana: "Pay {0}." The opening choices: "Play or draw?", answered Play or Draw, and "Keep or mulligan?" over Arena's own buttons. Catalogs: "Choose Creature Type", "Choose Card Name". Waterbend: "Tap permanents to Waterbend". What a declared creature is aimed at: "Choose attack target", "Choose what to block". Piles of a split: "Hand", "Exile", "Battlefield". The pass button's captions for where Arena shows none: "To Untap", "To Upkeep", "To Main 1", "To Main 2", "To Cleanup", "Nothing to play" under a halt and "To Opponent's Turn" under the player's own End Turn. The own-target warning (exception 7) asks Arena's question less its end, "Do you want to target {name}?", and a spell picked on the stack reads "Target {name}", or the warning's question where it is the player's own.

arena.does: Only the opponent's manifest dread, fateseal and put-back are seen, and games begin with the first player chosen.

entries.name: The phone
entries.rule: It plays what the desktop plays; its layout and gestures are Beryl's own. Every motion is one of the desktop's verbs between the phone's places. A card flies between your hand's fan, the stack in the middle band and its row; the opponent's leaves and joins the card backs at the top edge. A draw leaves the library's pile in its player's strip, and a card put into a graveyard lands on that pile. An ability lifts out of its source to the stack, and a token appears in its row. The rows make room as the middle band grows for the stack, so a source glides aside while its ability lifts. An exiled card rests unseen under its owner's graveyard, and an emblem's ability appears on the stack with no lift: the phone draws no exile pile and no emblem yet. Sounds follow the same steps. What the desktop shows around its table is composed for the phone from the same pieces. The menu button opens the settings with the log and the bug report in them. Undo and full control's mark stand at the end of the middle band, across from the phase. Unspent mana lies beside its player's life total, and the combat damage on its way on the total's rim. A touch on a graveyard, or on a library with a known card, lists its cards; a touch on a card shows it whole, and a touch beside it puts it away. The turn's banner crosses the middle band, a combat step's lies under the opponent's strip, and a scry's pill beside its player's lands, past the end of their row; a coin is tossed just above the middle band. A prompt picked on the table is the desktop's: the button it puts forward stands in the player's strip where the turn button is, with the one that passes on beside it; what it asks is a pill over that strip, and its other buttons are stacked over the turn button. A touch on a card the prompt can use uses it, and one it has no use for shows the card whole; a card in your hand is read by a touch and played by carrying it out of the hand. The Revealed Cards lie in the opponent's strip beside their graveyard, at a pile's size with no pill, and a touch opens them as it opens a pile.

verbs.name: fly
verbs.shows: A card travels from where it is to its new place, and flashes as it lands on the battlefield: a land played, a spell cast, a permanent spell resolving, a draw, a discard, an aura onto its permanent. One whose face changes turns over on the way, top over bottom and seen in depth: a spell is edge-on a little past half way and lands face up, a drawn card turns over as it leaves the library and flies face up, and one that lay the other way up the table never spins round besides. A card you draw alone is held up large to be read and then drops into the hand; each of several drawn together rises over the table, clear of the cards held, and comes down into its place, the hand having made room for them all as the first left. A card that lands face down the other way up the table, as the opponent's draw does, leaves the way up it will lie. A spell cast and a permanent resolving leave the straight line in a shallow arc that bows toward their controller's edge of the table, the permanent leaning a little into it.

arena.does: A played land glides from where it is released to its slot in about 0.4 s. The opponent's spell leaves their hand as a card back and is face up when it reaches the stack, about 0.4 s; the player's own flies from where it is released in about 0.35 s. A resolving permanent flies to its slot in about 0.6 s and the slot flashes. A drawn card leaves the library turning face up within about 0.2 s, flies large beside the stack, holds about 0.2 s and drops into the hand, about 1.1 s in all; three drawn by one spell leave a quarter second apart and fly the same way with no hold, about 0.7 s each. A discard drops to the graveyard at hand size in about 0.2 s.

verbs.name: appear
verbs.shows: A card comes to be at its place with no flight: a token, the opening hand, a card a look put in the graveyard. Its row makes room in its delay, so it shows at a place already open.

arena.does: A token appears whole with a short glow, a batch as one group. The opening hand and a mulligan's new hand are there at once.

verbs.name: vanish
verbs.shows: A card or an ability goes from where it is with no flight, and a card is at its new place as it is gone: destroyed, exiled, sacrificed, countered, returned to a hand, or done resolving. Its step is its going alone; what it left room for closes up after, as one move even where the going is a cut, and where nothing does the next thing follows at once.

arena.does: A destroyed permanent falls to ash in about 1 s, an exiled one becomes a vortex, a sacrificed one flashes, and a returned one glows and is gone; none flies to a pile or a hand. A countered spell crumbles on the stack. A resolved instant darkens and dissolves there, or shrinks into its graveyard. A finished ability is gone between two frames.

verbs.name: emerge
verbs.shows: An ability lifts out of its source and goes on the stack, along a shallow arc that bows toward its controller's edge of the table. The source stays as it is.

arena.does: A small copy of the card appears on the source and travels along a curve to the stack, growing, in 0.25 to 0.35 s; an activated ability does the same. Two triggers of one event leave 0.3 s apart. A dies trigger leaves before its source breaks up.

verbs.name: flip
verbs.shows: A card turns over where it lies: a double-faced card transforms, a face-down permanent turns face up (not seen: built as "A card turning face up" says).

arena.does: A transforming card is covered by an effect (a lava slab, a cocoon) for about 1.1 s and shows its new face as the effect clears; it neither turns nor grows.

verbs.name: tap
verbs.shows: A permanent turns a quarter as it taps or untaps, its whole card about its own middle where it lies. Its row then closes up or makes room, the tapped apart from the untapped.

arena.does: Arena tilts a tapped permanent's art crop 7 to 8 degrees in about 0.2 s and dims it; an untap restores it in about 0.1 s.

verbs.name: strike
verbs.shows: A creature pulls back, lunges at what it deals combat damage to, which flashes as the blow lands, and draws back; a player's life total changes on that blow. Two creatures that strike each other meet half way, at one time. A strike that would pass over a creature of an earlier strike still on its way out or back waits until that one is home. On something much smaller than itself it lands whole, shrinking as it goes.

arena.does: Each attacker winds back, lunges from its row to the player's avatar or to its blocker, the screen flashes, and it drifts back, 0.65 to 1.3 s in all. A blocked attacker strikes about 0.4 s before an unblocked one. First strike is a strike of its own, seconds earlier.

verbs.name: streak
verbs.shows: A streak of light leaves one thing and lands on another, which flashes: mana from its source into the spell or ability it pays for, and damage from a spell or ability to what it hits. It rises out of its source's row toward the middle of the table on a low arc, a bright head with a tail behind it, gathering as it leaves and quickening all the way, and its tail is drawn in as it lands. Mana leaves as its source begins to turn, several into one spell together, and has left the row before the row closes up; the mana of a pile of lands fans out to either side. A source with no place left on the table sends none: what its mana pays for only flashes.

arena.does: Each tapped land sends one streak of its color to the spell on the stack in about 0.3 s. A burn spell or ability glows, and a streak of fire crosses to its target in about 0.25 s, with a burst where it lands; the spell leaves after.

verbs.name: count
verbs.shows: A number changes and shows that it did: a life total, a kind of counter, a power and toughness, a mana pool.

arena.does: A life total jumps to its new value in a burst of about 0.4 s; a loss's red number drifts down from the opponent's avatar, and a gain's green one rises for about 0.5 s. A counter's badge settles onto its permanent after a flash. A planeswalker's loyalty changes about a second after its ability reaches the stack.

verbs.name: set
verbs.shows: The table changes and nothing moves: a step of the turn begins, a library is shuffled, a permanent's characteristics change.

arena.does: Nothing animates as a step begins, and nothing shows on a library when it is shuffled.

verbs.name: showcase
verbs.shows: A card an effect reveals is held up for both players to read: its face joins the "Revealed Cards" pile at the top left, growing into its place there, and the card itself lies where it was.

arena.does: Revealed cards gather under a "Revealed Cards" pill at the top left, each growing into place in about 0.2 s. A click on the pile opens a browser of them under the same words, with a Done button, and the pile stays afterward until the cross on its pill puts it away.

verbs.name: dwell
verbs.shows: Nothing moves while something is read: the opponent's spell or ability, before it resolves unanswered, and the table as the game ends, before the result covers it.

arena.does: The opponent's spell sits on the stack for 0.7 to 1.9 s before it resolves. After the play that ends a game the table stays in view about 3 s, the loser's avatar bursting for the first half of it, before the result covers it.

verbs.name: announce
verbs.shows: A notice passes over the table: the turn banner, the pill that says what a scry did, a coin tossed. Play goes on under the banner and the pill, which are drawn over the cards in flight and fade in, stand and fade out, the banner sinking toward its player as it goes. A coin is waited for, and has the table to itself: it is thrown only once the turn's banner has gone, mid-table, rises a diameter and a half toward the viewer turning fast, falls back onto its plate quickening, lands with a swell and a flare, and only then says who won, which stands for the rest of its step.

arena.does: "Your Turn" or "Opponent's Turn" glows at the centre for about a second while cards move under it. A pill above an avatar reads "Scry: 1 top, 1 bottom." for about 3 s. A coin a card flips is tossed mid-table and lands in about 1.2 s.

verbs.name: point
verbs.shows: An arrow or line between two things, from the step that begins it to the step that ends it: to a target, from an ability to its source, from an attacker to what it attacks, from a blocker to its attacker. Each is drawn as light, a ribbon with a hot core. An arrow at a target is a bowed arc, a thread at its spell that swells to a spear head, which strikes out of its spell or ability once that has landed on the stack, lands with a flash and sparks, and has light run along it toward its target while it stands. It comes onto a card from the open table in front of it, never along its row, and its head lies on the card's face; at a player it goes over the top onto their life total; between two things that all but touch it goes round their side. One at the stack item its own lies over leaves the side of its own item and comes round into the end of the other's strip, its head on the table beside the stack, pointing at that item's name. The line to a source is the same arc, thin and faint with no head, and stretches as the ability lifts. A line of combat is a straight beam that narrows to a dart, from the tip of the wedge an attacker wears, or from a blocker's edge to the tip of its attacker's wedge. Each is one line for as long as it lasts, drawn every moment from where its two ends are, and an arrow or a line of combat drains into what it points at over the step that ends it, which waits until it has stood whole for its end's delay, so that one whose spell resolves at once is still read, and which what follows waits for, so that neither end moves under it. An ability and the line to its source stay a moment after what the ability did, and go in one tick. An arrow at a target and the line to a source are over everything at rest and under what flies. A line of combat lies on the table, under the cards and the step's banner, as an attacker's wedge and a blocker's crescent do: it passes behind a creature that stands in its way. A browser with no WebGL draws each as a path instead.

arena.does: A cyan arc runs from a spell or ability to its target until it resolves. A thin line joins an ability to its source from the frame it lifts. A thin gold line runs from a blocker to its attacker until combat damage is done. An attacker has no line to the player, only its chevron.

verbs.name: mark
verbs.shows: A mark from the list below on a card, an ability or a player, from the step that begins it to the step that ends it. The light of what may be picked comes up over a moment, on all of it at once. Every other mark is there in the tick its step begins, so that one which takes another's place on a card swaps with it, and each is gone as the step that ends it begins.

verbs.name: lift
verbs.shows: Cards the opponent is handling come away from their pile, face down, from the step that begins the look to the step that ends it. Cards the player's own prompt holds up come away from where they lie into its tray, face up, as the prompt opens; lie as each click sorts them; and go back to where the table has them as the first steps of what the answer did begin.

arena.does: Cards the opponent scries come off their library face down at its size and lie beside it.

effects.name: glow
effects.shows: A halo of warm light around a card, bright at once, that spreads and fades: the card is new here, is leaving whole, or sends a streak. On the stack, where the spell that acts on a card lies over it, the light is a rim inside the card's own frame.

effects.name: settle
effects.shows: A wash of light over a card and a halo around it, bright as it lands and gone as it settles.

effects.name: dissolve
effects.shows: A card darkens, holds dark, and then breaks up along a stippled edge from the top down, for as long as its step: it is destroyed, countered or sacrificed.

effects.name: dim
effects.shows: A card darkens whole and fades where it lies, for as long as its step: a spell that has resolved is done.

effects.name: blanch
effects.shows: A card is lost in white light, for as long as its step: it is going to exile.

effects.name: cover
effects.shows: A veil of light closes over a card, hides it while it changes, and clears from what it now is, for as long as its step.

effects.name: impact
effects.shows: A burst of hot light on what a creature strikes or a streak of damage hits, a card or a player's life total, whole as the blow lands and spreading as it fades.

effects.name: flash
effects.shows: A flare of pale light over a spell or ability as the mana that pays for it lands, whole at once and gone as it spreads.

effects.name: pulse
effects.shows: A ring of light round a card's frame while its numbers swell and settle: a counter put on it or taken off, its loyalty, its power and toughness.

effects.name: loss
effects.shows: A life total flares red, and the number that says how much it lost sinks away from it and fades, for as long as its step.

effects.name: gain
effects.shows: A life total flares green, and the number that says how much it gained rises from it and fades, for as long as its step.

marks.name: eligible
marks.means: The player may pick or use it now: a card to play, a permanent with an ability, a legal target, an attacker or blocker to declare, an option.

arena.does: Arena outlines all of these in one cyan, and neither dims nor outlines what cannot be picked.

marks.name: selected
marks.means: The player has picked it in the open prompt.

arena.does: A clicked attacker and a chosen blocker turn gold.

marks.name: suggested
marks.means: The offered default would use it: a permanent Auto Pay would tap, the blocker the session would deal lethal damage to next.
marks.look: An ember ring. Not seen in Arena.

marks.name: paying
marks.look: The permanent turns and carries a tap mark, with no outline. Not seen in Arena.

marks.name: hostile-target
marks.means: A target its chooser does not control.
